Watching this reminds me of when my children were in high school competitions.  They always chose music that the teacher said was too complicated because it was collegiate level.  Every time, they excelled and went to state finals for trumpet and French horn based upon two aspects of advice that I gave them that they admitted helped them:  1) Do it so that you can prove your teacher wrong.  2)  Don't be nervous since none of the judges will remember who you are in a week, so it doesn't matter, make this a day of satisfaction and joy for yourself.  I also told them to play as if this is the last 10 minutes the earth exists and to put your own flair and passion into each note.  They were so casual and smiling while other students would be in tears.  I felt badly for those kids that succumbed to that pressure.
